headline: 251 prisoners died in custody during first nine months of 2026
summary: Overcrowding and poor medical care in Bangladesh's prisons are leading to preventable deaths, as seen in the case of Rafiqul Islam.
details: Rafiqul Islam, 59, died after a three-hour delay in being taken to the hospital from Dhaka Central Jail. He had a history of heart disease and diabetes, requiring regular medication and check-ups.
Rafiqul is one of at least 251 prisoners who died in custody during the first nine months of 2026, most of whom died in outside hospitals or while being transported.
Prison authorities state these deaths are typically illness-related, while human rights activists argue that medical care in prisons is almost non-existent and a violation of human rights.
Data shows 1,413 deaths in custody between 2021 and 2025, with the vast majority occurring outside prison hospitals.
Prisons are currently facing severe overcrowding. The system, designed for 45,186 people, held over 110,000 prisoners by mid-October 2026.
The prison department attributes the increase in population to more arrests for maintaining law and order and delays in securing bail.

headline: Farmer killed in Chattogram after refusing extortion
summary: A 50-year-old farmer's body was found on a road in Rangunia, with both hands severed up to the elbows.
details: Police recovered the body of 50-year-old Nezam Uddin from the Kalichari Bridge area of Mirkhil village in Rangunia, Chattogram, on Wednesday morning.
The victim's two hands were found severed up to the elbows and lying beside the body on a paved road, approximately 1.5 kilometers away from his paddy field.
Nezam Uddin had gone to guard his crops from wild elephants on Tuesday afternoon but failed to return home, leading his family to find him the following morning.
Family members alleged that terrorists had recently demanded extortion money from Nezam Uddin in connection with the construction of a house.
According to South Rangunia Police Station OC Mo. Hilal Uddin Ahmed, preliminary investigations suggest the victim died from excessive blood loss after being attacked with sharp weapons.
Police have sent the body for an autopsy and are continuing their investigation to identify and arrest the the perpetrators of the murder.
caption:
A farmer in Chattogram was found dead with both hands severed—family alleges it was over refusing to pay extortion money.

Police recovered the body of 50-year-old Nezam Uddin from the Kalichari Bridge area of Mirkhil village in Rangunia, Chattogram, on Wednesday morning.

The victim's two hands were found severed up to the elbows and lying beside the body on a paved road, approximately 1.5 kilometers away from his paddy field.

Nezam Uddin had gone to guard his crops from wild elephants on Tuesday afternoon but failed to return home, leading his family to find him the following morning.

Family members alleged that terrorists had recently demanded extortion money from Nezam Uddin in connection with the construction of a house.

According to South Rangunia Police Station OC Mo. Hilal Uddin Ahmed, preliminary investigations suggest the victim died from excessive blood loss after being attacked with sharp weapons.

Police have sent the body for an autopsy and are continuing their investigation to identify and arrest the the perpetrators of the murder.
